learnings: parseSearchQuery/buildTsQuery/searchDocuments live in packages/sql/src/{search-query,search,snippet}.ts; 61 new unit tests in src/__tests__/{search-query,search,search-performance}.test.ts, 162 green in the package. Search over 5000 documents measures 27-34 ms against a 300 ms budget (page query + count query + snippets), so SM-43 passes with an order of magnitude to spare. The parse keeps an ordered `clauses: SearchClause[]` rather than separate `terms`/`groups` fields — a clause of one term is a required word or phrase, a clause of several is an OR group — because the order is what tells buildTsQuery which word the user is still typing. `document.tsv` stores the title as written and the 'simple' configuration does not unaccent, so diacritic insensitivity comes from the fuzzy title branch (`similarity(title_fold, freeText)`), not from full-text matching; the titles scope therefore matches `to_tsvector(title_fold)` against a folded tsquery (`buildTsQuery(parsed, { fold: true })`). An exclusion is a top-level NOT over `document.tsv` in addition to the `!` inside the tsquery, because the `!` cannot reach a document that was found through its title or through a qualifier. Snippet marks are U+0002/U+0003 handed to ts_headline as StartSel/StopSel and split by `snippetSegments` — never markup. An invalid regex throws SearchRegexInvalidError before any statement runs, so the interface can keep the previous list (APP-01-05-FE 9). No plugin, instance or VFS file was touched.
